title: 06b-B T3: composeArcSummary accepts a bible parameter
description:
Objective:
Add a required `bible: CampaignBibleInput` parameter to composeArcSummary. The system prompt and user message both incorporate the bible so the arc summary can reference NPCs/factions canonically. Update the existing arcSummary tests to pass a bible argument. Add a new test that asserts bible content lands in the user prompt. Update play.ts's call site to pass an empty CampaignBibleInput placeholder (T4 will replace this with the extracted bible).

Files:
- Modify: packages/core/src/memory/arcSummary.ts
- Modify: packages/core/test/arcSummary.test.ts
- Modify: packages/cli/src/play.ts

Steps:
1. In packages/core/src/memory/arcSummary.ts:
   a. Import CampaignBibleInput from './summary.js'.
   b. Add `bible: CampaignBibleInput` to ComposeArcSummaryInput.
   c. Add an extra line to ARC_SUMMARY_SYSTEM_PROMPT instructing the model to reference the bible's NPCs/factions canonically (see Design).
   d. Replace the existing `renderRecaps(input.recaps)` call with a new helper that joins `renderBible(input.bible)` and `renderRecaps(input.recaps)`.
   e. Add the renderBible helper (see Design).
2. In packages/core/test/arcSummary.test.ts:
   a. Add a small EMPTY_BIBLE constant and a NON_EMPTY_BIBLE constant (see Design).
   b. Update each of the 4 existing tests to pass a `bible:` argument (EMPTY_BIBLE for happy-path; NON_EMPTY_BIBLE wherever assertions check the rendered prompt).
   c. Add a new test 'renders the campaign bible into the user prompt' (see Design).
3. In packages/cli/src/play.ts, in rollupCampaignArc's call to composeArcSummary, add a placeholder `bible: { worldFacts: [], majorNpcs: [], factions: [], openThreads: [] }` argument. This is a temporary placeholder that T4 immediately replaces with the extracted bible.
4. Run: npx vitest run --reporter=verbose
   Expected: all tests pass (arcSummary suite has 5 tests now: 2 originally-happy + 2 originally-failure + 1 new bible-render test).
5. Run: npm run typecheck. Expected: success.
6. Commit:
     git add packages/core/src/memory/arcSummary.ts packages/core/test/arcSummary.test.ts packages/cli/src/play.ts
     git commit -m "composeArcSummary accepts a campaign bible parameter (loreweaver-5ze)"
acceptance_criteria:
1. ComposeArcSummaryInput includes a required `bible: CampaignBibleInput` field.
2. composeArcSummary's user message renders a '## campaign bible' section before the session recaps; each bucket (worldFacts/majorNpcs/factions/openThreads) renders as a list or '(none)'.
3. The arcSummary system prompt instructs the model to reference the bible canonically.
4. packages/core/test/arcSummary.test.ts contains 5 tests (existing 4 updated + 1 new bible-render test); all pass.
5. packages/cli/src/play.ts passes a placeholder empty bible to composeArcSummary so the typecheck stays green; this placeholder is documented as temporary in the commit message.
6. npm run typecheck and npx vitest run both succeed (full suite).
7. The commit message references loreweaver-5ze.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text:
Code review summary for `4f288b3..329049c`:

Assessment: Ready to merge

Critical: none
Important: none
Minor: The `renderBible` helper hardcodes the four bucket names as display strings (e.g. `### majorNpcs`). If `CampaignBibleInput` gains a fifth field, `renderBible` silently omits it. Consider deriving from `Object.entries(bible)` or adding a compile-time exhaustiveness check. Low urgency given T4 owns the extraction path.
Follow-up: T4 (replace empty-bible placeholder in play.ts with extracted bible); consider ordering the bucket keys derivation if the type stabilises.
